With vaccinations progressing and policy support still strong, activity and employment continue to firm, and the FOMC is tapering asset purchases while keeping the policy rate at 0–0.25 percent to preserve accommodative financial conditions and anchor inflation expectations near 2 percent. That said, the Federal Reserve’s Financial Stability Report highlights elevated vulnerabilities that temper the otherwise constructive outlook: asset valuations appear stretched in some markets with compressed risk premia; liquidity and maturity mismatches persist in money market and open‑end bond funds; Treasury market fragilities remain a focus; nonbank leverage and cyber risks are notable; and pandemic‑sensitive CRE (for example, office and lodging) still faces pressure. Banks remain well capitalized and household balance sheets are generally solid, supporting credit intermediation. Balancing these positives against elevated inflation and the vulnerabilities cited in the FSR, the outlook is cautiously optimistic but more guarded than a purely macro read would suggest.
